document_check.note: Alvi et al., Knowledge-Based Systems 248 (2022) 108815, 'A deep learning based framework for diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment'. Public EEG dataset of 27 subjects (11 MCI, 16 normal), 8,100 six-second segments, GRU accuracy 95.51 +/- 3.11 % under 5-fold cross-validation (Table 2). Matches the cited study and numbers.

cited_result: GRU classifier distinguishing MCI from healthy-control EEG: accuracy 95.51 +/- 3.11 % under 5-fold cross-validation over 8,100 segments from 27 participants (Table 2).
tool_reason: The cited result is the accuracy of a deep-learning diagnostic classifier, a prediction-model performance question covered by PROBAST with the PROBAST+AI considerations.

domains.rationale: A convenience public dataset of 11 MCI and 16 normal participants with separately defined groups (case-control-type sampling), recruitment not described, and exclusion of people with serious medical or psychiatric illness.

signalling.question: 1.1 Were appropriate data sources used (e.g. cohort, RCT or nested case-control data)?
signalling.quote: This MCI study has exercised a publicly available EEG dataset of 27 subjects from the Sina and Nour Hospital, Isfahan, Iran [31, 36]. 16 normal and 11 MCI subjects were part of this EEG data collection.

signalling.question: 1.2 Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?
signalling.quote: None of these 27 subjects had head trauma, dementia, and a history of major psychiatric disorders, serious medical disease, and substance misuse.

domains.rationale: Every participant had the same standardised resting EEG protocol. Features were learned automatically from the signals, which are available at the time of intended use.

signalling.question: 2.1 Were predictors defined and assessed in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: For each of the subject, recording lasted for 30 min and signals were digitized using 32 channel EEG device with a sampling frequency of 256 Hz

signalling.question: 2.2 Were predictor assessments made without knowledge of outcome data?
signalling.quote: For feature extraction, no separate method is used, and for classification, four different machine learning (ML) models are tested with the processed EEG dataset.

signalling.question: 2.3 Are all predictors available at the time the model is intended to be used?
signalling.quote: All subjects were instructed to close their eyes, feel relaxed and conscious to avoid drowsiness during the EEG recordings.

domains.rationale: Petersen's criteria are named, but the reference standard is described only as an MMSE 'neuropsychiatric interview'. The stated MMSE range for MCI (21 to 26) conflicts with Table 1 (27.6 +/- 0.9). Blinding and timing are not reported.

signalling.question: 3.2 Was a pre-specified or standard outcome definition used?
signalling.quote: was performed for each of the subject following the Petersen’s criteria.

signalling.quote: interview also known as Mini-mental state examination (MMSE) was performed for each of the subject following the Petersen’s criteria. (EEG is not described as part of the diagnosis.)

domains.rationale: There are only 11 participants with MCI. The 300 segments per participant were split at segment level (70/20/10 and 5-fold CV) with no subject-wise separation, so segments from one person appear on both sides. Architectures and hyperparameters were chosen through repeated experiments for the best result, there is no calibration, and the reported metrics are internally inconsistent.

applicability.rationale: Only 27 people from a single hospital dataset, with comorbidity excluded.
The MCI reference standard is poorly described and internally inconsistent.

overall_rationale: Participants (domain 1) and analysis (domain 4) are high. The dataset is a tiny case-control-type public sample with 11 MCI participants. Cross-validation over 8,100 segments from 27 people without a subject-wise split almost certainly leaks participant identity into the test folds. Tuning relied on repeated experiments, and there is no calibration or external validation. Outcome (domain 3) is unclear.
